questions.q: In this capstone's deployment, what role does the vLLM server play?
options: It only stores the model weights on disk
It is the OpenAI-compatible HTTP server that owns the model, the request scheduler, and the KV cache
It replaces the need for a GPU entirely
It is strictly a load balancer with no model logic
questions.explain: vLLM exposes an OpenAI-compatible endpoint and owns the model, scheduling, and KV cache management on the GPU it runs on.

questions.q: Why does the launch command cap `--max-model-len` at 8192 instead of using Llama 3.1's full 128K context?
options: vLLM does not support contexts longer than 8192 tokens
Anchorline's requests don't need 128K of context, and a lower cap frees KV-cache memory for more concurrent requests
Llama 3.1 8B cannot generate more than 8192 tokens total, ever
It is a required default that cannot be changed
questions.explain: The cap matches the actual use case (a question plus pasted logs) and frees up GPU memory that would otherwise be reserved for KV cache on requests that will never use the full window.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT something you need a separate flag to turn on in vLLM, because it is already the default behavior?
options: Continuous batching
PagedAttention-based KV cache management
Setting the server's listening port
Both continuous batching and PagedAttention are on by default
questions.explain: Continuous batching and PagedAttention are vLLM's default scheduling and KV-cache strategy — flags like --max-num-seqs tune how aggressively they run rather than switching them on.

options: It quantizes the model weights to INT4
It splits a long prompt's prefill work into chunks interleaved with other requests' decode steps, so one long prompt doesn't stall everyone else
It increases the model's context window beyond its architectural maximum
It disables the KV cache
questions.explain: Chunked prefill interleaves prefill chunks for long prompts with decode steps for other in-flight requests, improving fairness under mixed request lengths.

questions.q: After starting the server, what does a successful curl request to the chat completions endpoint confirm?
options: Nothing useful — curl cannot test an inference server
That the model loaded, the scheduler is accepting requests, and KV cache allocation succeeded
That the GPU has reached 100% memory utilization
That autoscaling is correctly configured
questions.explain: A real response with the expected choices structure is a smoke test that the three things most likely to be silently broken after a deploy — model load, scheduler, and KV cache allocation — all came up clean.
